clue.text: Desperate character, daughter (23) getting collared — it doesn't look good

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the strongman of the British comic The Dandy
the solution to 23 down is a card-game word; to play one is to ruff, and a ruff is also a frilled collar

explanation.surface: A desperate figure, a daughter being arrested — not a good look for the family.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a cartoon character from the British comic The Dandy. 23 down means play a winning card, which in bridge is to ruff, and a ruff is an Elizabethan collar, so 'getting collared' fits too.
explanation.definitionFit: Flakes of scalp on the shoulders are notoriously unsightly, so this is a playful description of the condition.

parts.note: read as P for President and 45 for the number in sequence: the 45th US President, who also served as the 47th

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a P45 is the tax form handed to someone leaving a job, the puzzle's theme. Here it is read as 'President no. 45'.
explanation.definitionFit: The forty-fifth holder of the American presidency was the property tycoon from New York who took office in 2017.

clue.text: In action, rolled American tobacco

indicators.note: rolled suggests a cigarette, but here the letters of the two words are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rolls a cigarette from US tobacco while busy doing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled' turns IN ACTION into NICOTIAN; A for American follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the botanical genus of the tobacco plant, also grown as a fragrant ornamental flower.

clue.text: In which, when it's your round, you'll be under the table

definitions.text: In which, when it's your round, you'll be under the table

parts.words: In which, when it's your round, you'll be under the table
parts.note: a round sounds like buying drinks at the pub, and 'under the table' like being drunk; really it is a bullet in a revolver chamber that leaves you dead

explanation.walkthrough: The pub reading (your round of drinks, ending up under the table) hides a deadly game with a revolver: the 'round' is the bullet, and you end up slumped dead.
explanation.definitionFit: In this lethal game of chance, players take turns firing a revolver with one live cartridge at their own head.

clue.text: Female fell behind, tired

parts.note: to lag is to fall behind

explanation.surface: A woman fell behind the group because she was worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to lose energy, so someone who has flagged has grown weary.

clue.text: Pass by il Duomo regularly providing refuge

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of these words is taken, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A tourist strolls past Florence's cathedral, which offers sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the 2nd, 4th, 6th... letters of PASSBYILDUOMO. Il Duomo is the Italian name for a city's cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: This is protection or shelter granted to someone fleeing danger, as in political sanctuary.

clue.text: Black coffee Sean spilled at work could mean P45

indicators.note: spilled says the letters of these words are splashed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Sean knocks his black coffee over the office desk and could be fired for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A P45 is the British tax form an employee receives on leaving a job, so here it means dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdemeanour serious enough to justify dismissal is one an employer can fire you for.

clue.text: "Vassal state" falsely, say, taken over?

parts.note: to state something falsely is to lie

indicators.note: taken over in a down clue means the letters are turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: say means 'for example', abbreviated as e.g.

explanation.surface: A puppet state, so called falsely, perhaps conquered by another power?
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken over' in a down clue turns the abbreviation upwards. 'Vassal state' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Vassal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The term has been used both for a feudal lord and for the vassal who owed him allegiance.

clue.text: St. David's Day: new government demands P45

parts.note: St David's Day, the Welsh national day, is 1 March, written MARCH I in Roman numerals
demands are orders or commands

explanation.surface: On Wales's national day the new administration insists on someone's dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: St David is the patron saint of Wales; his day falls on 1 March, giving MARCH plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent packing from a job is idiomatically being told to march off, matching the British leaving form.

clue.text: Senior citizens retch, initially horrified over P45

parts.note: old people as a group are the old
to retch is to heave

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Elderly people are sick with shock on being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls, written O on scorecards. A P45 is the British form issued on leaving a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the push from employment is colloquially being given a forceful shove out of the door.

clue.text: Steals tops from Next, Intimissimi, Calvin Klein, Selfridge's

indicators.note: tops from means the leading letter of each of these store and brand names is taken

explanation.surface: A shoplifter pinches tops from a string of high-street and designer clothing brands.
explanation.walkthrough: Next and Selfridges are British department and high-street stores; Intimissimi and Calvin Klein are fashion brands. 'tops' looks like clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to nick something is to pilfer it.

clue.text: Swift retribution seen from Bath chicken farm getting exposed

indicators.note: getting exposed means each word loses its outer layer, its first and last letter, leaving the inside

explanation.surface: A chicken farm near Bath is publicly shamed and suffers punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting exposed' strips the ends from BATH, CHICKEN and FARM, leaving AT, HICKE and AR. Bath is an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip round the ear is quick, informal punishment; the idiom promises a cuff that leaves the ear swollen.

clue.text: Revolting Rees-Mogg (nit!) telephoned about issuing P45

indicators.note: Revolting says the hidden letters are read backwards
about here means the letters lie around in the words that follow, held within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The appalling Jacob Rees-Mogg, a fool, rang to sack someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'about issuing P' cut the clue mid-number; the definition is 'issuing P45' (dismissing staff), and 'about' signals the hidden letters. 'Revolting' reverses OGGNITTEL. Rees-Mogg is a British Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Releasing an employee from a job is dismissing them, which is when a P45 tax form is handed over.

clue.text: First in a series: "beer, and where to find it"

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
beer is found in a pub, and PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: A pub crawl's opening line: beer, and directions to where it is served.
explanation.walkthrough: PH marks a public house on British Ordnance Survey maps.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the opening letter of the Hebrew alphabet, so it heads that series of characters.

clue.text: Boring, soporific Anne Diamond given P45

indicators.note: Boring means drilling into the words that follow to find the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A dull TV presenter, Anne Diamond, has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like a dig at the presenter but signals the hidden letters. Anne Diamond is a British breakfast-TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech someone who has been fired from a job has been tinned, or sacked.

clue.text: Lundgren, at home, is a fairly blubbery individual

parts.note: Dolph Lundgren is the Swedish action-film actor
to be at home is to be in

explanation.surface: The action star Lundgren, relaxing at home, is getting a bit flabby.
explanation.definitionFit: This marine mammal has a layer of insulating fat, though less than a whale.

clue.text: Beautiful girl head over heels enthralled by revolutionary hero, one bearing flowers

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside the following piece
revolutionary means the letters of the next word are overturned and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: head over heels means turned upside down, so in a down entry the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful young woman

explanation.surface: A lovely girl falls head over heels for a revolutionary hero, who brings her flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head over heels' looks like love but turns the girl upside down; 'revolutionary' rearranges the hero to HORE, which then wraps round her.
explanation.definitionFit: This winter-flowering plant, also called the Christmas rose, produces blooms.

clue.text: Encourage to send up one in the kitchen cabinet?

parts.note: to egg someone on is to encourage them

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to remit is to send, as with money

explanation.surface: A political adviser is urged to dispatch a member of the inner circle of ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses REMIT. 'Kitchen cabinet' is an informal name for a leader's circle of unofficial advisers.
explanation.definitionFit: A small timing device for boiling eggs is a gadget you might keep in a kitchen cupboard.

clue.text: At last, Bing and Dorothy get together … va-va-voom!

indicators.note: At last means only the final letter of the following word is used

parts.note: Dorothy Lamour starred with Bing Crosby and Bob Hope in the Road films

explanation.surface: Bing Crosby and Dorothy Lamour finally pair up, and the result is sexy.
explanation.walkthrough: Bing Crosby and Dorothy Lamour co-starred in the 1940s Road to ... comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Va-va-voom is slang for alluring sex appeal and excitement, the same quality as allure.

clue.text: Rangers overwhelm Celtic from the off, starting "Old Firm" in flamboyant style

indicators.note: from the off means only the opening letter of each of these words counts
starting means just the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Glasgow derby: Rangers crush Celtic from kick-off, opening the Old Firm match in showy fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers and Celtic are the two big Glasgow football clubs, whose rivalry is called the Old Firm.
explanation.definitionFit: This 18th-century decorative style is known for its ornate, elaborate curves and frills.

clue.text: Ballyhoo in America as much-loved bear returns to Los Angeles

indicators.note: returns means the bear's name comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is the beloved children's bear

explanation.surface: There's a fuss in the US as a favourite bear comes back to Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage this word means fuss or noisy publicity, matching the sense of excitement and hype.

clue.text: See 9
See 8
Write off oil company

definitions.meaning: to wreck a car beyond repair, in informal usage
the French energy giant of that name

explanation.definitionFit: To total a vehicle is to destroy it; the French oil major also trades under that word.

clue.text: See 1
Switzerland: "Gold, francs, €; it's what drives us"

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
FF is the abbreviation for French francs
EUR is the currency code for the euro

explanation.surface: A Swiss banker says money — gold, francs, euros — is what motivates us.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired driver is the person whose job is to drive us around.

clue.text: So much tea brewed for Fu Manchu?

indicators.note: brewed means the letters of these words are stewed together and mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone brews so much tea for Fu Manchu, the fictional Chinese villain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fu Manchu is a long, drooping style of facial hair named after the fictional villain; '?' marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fu Manchu is a style of upper-lip whiskers, so it is an example of this facial hair.

clue.text: Slipknot shortly retiring, heading east

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: shortly means soon

indicators.note: heading means only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: The band Slipknot will soon be calling it a day and heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: Slipknot, a US heavy-metal band, looks like the subject; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A running loop that tightens when pulled is a slipknot of this kind, as on a hangman's rope.

clue.text: I heard one covering hip-hop artist

indicators.note: I heard says the word sounds like the one in the grid

parts.note: something that covers or encloses is a wrapper

explanation.surface: Someone says they heard a person covered a hip-hop star's song.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent W of the covering word drops out in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A hip-hop performer delivers rhythmic spoken lyrics, the genre's core performer.

clue.text: Sleeping rough, hovels give me accommodation for a shilling

indicators.note: accommodation means the hovels take in and house the next word

parts.note: a hole is a squalid, poky dwelling
S is the abbreviation for a shilling in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A rough sleeper is offered a bed in a slum for a shilling a night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation' puts ME inside HOLES. The shilling was an old British coin worth 12 old pence, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without a roof over their head is sleeping rough, out on the streets.
